title: Cytokine dysregulation and hippocampal neurogenesis: A shared mechanism underlying cognitive impairments across neuropsychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders.
abstract: Neuropsychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders, such as major depressive disorder, bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, Alzheimer's disease, and Parkinson's disease, all show a neuroimmune signature with dysregulated inflammatory cytokine profile and cognitive impairment. Although these deficits are clinically relevant, the immunological mechanisms that cause cognitive dysfunction across these conditions remain poorly defined. Recent studies demonstrate that inflammatory cytokines actively modulate adult hippocampal neurogenesis, a process critical for learning, memory, and affective regulation. Here, we synthesise clinical evidence to characterise the disorder-specific inflammatory profile of each of these five disorders, representing each profile with three frequently dysregulated cytokines rather than a single cytokine signature shared across conditions. We also integrate preclinical data where cytokines induce behavioural, cognitive, and hippocampal-related deficits in animal and cellular models. Hence, this review develops a mechanistic framework that links brain-immune communication directly to cognitive impairment through hippocampal neurogenesis, thereby suggesting neuroimmune targets for therapeutic intervention.

title: A water-pinning hot spot drives templated tau aggregation.
abstract: Tau assembles into fibrillar aggregates that are pathological hallmarks of a group of neurodegenerative diseases collectively called tauopathies. Templated aggregation of naïve tau to seeding-competent fibrils that proceed from cell to cell is a key driver of prion-like progression of tauopathies. This study tests the hypothesis that tau, an intrinsically disordered protein, achieves in-register stacking to form seed-competent fibrils by a pinning action of tau to each other and/or the seed surface via a single dominant hotspot to avoid mismatch in tau stacking to fibrils. Structured solvation water has been proposed to be a signature of such hot spots at both the tau fibril-end surface and soluble tau monomers. Although jR2R3-P301L tau exhibits a heterogeneous hydration landscape in its intrinsically disordered state, with enhanced water structuring near the P301L mutation site, it is unclear whether a localized hotspot exists at the fibril end surface and surface water facilitates the initial contacts in templated aggregation. Using rapid 1H-15N SOFAST-HMQC NMR to track seed-induced aggregation of jR2R3-P301L in real time, complemented by molecular dynamics simulation of fibril surface hydration, we identify a residue-specific pinning hotspot that is prone to dewetting followed by sequential folding and incorporation of the remaining segment in a two-step dock-and-lock process. Site-specific spin labeling further demonstrates that blocking this pinning hotspot disrupts templated aggregation, leading to shorter fibrils. The identification of a dominant pinning site will facilitate the rational design of binders to effectively disrupt fibril extension or serve as diagnostic or therapeutic strategies.

title: A critical mechanistic synthesis of PINK1-mediated mitophagy signaling and its therapeutic targeting in Parkinson's disease neurodegeneration.
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder that is associated with loss of dopaminergic neurons, mitochondrial dysfunction and disruption of cellular homeostasis. PTEN-induced kinase 1 (PINK1) plays a crucial role in mitochondrial quality control by regulating mitophagy, mitochondrial dynamics, and calcium signaling to maintain neuronal bioenergetic homeostasis. This review critically evaluates the molecular pathways underlying PINK1-mediated mitochondrial integrity and the mechanisms by which loss-of-function mutations contribute to the pathogenesis of PD. Familial early-onset PD is strongly associated with pathogenic PINK1 mutations identified through genetic studies. Therapeutic approaches targeting the PINK1 pathway are examined, including adeno-associated virus (AAV)-based gene delivery, direct small-molecule PINK1 activation (MTK458), and indirect modulation of mitophagy and mitochondrial homeostasis by compounds such as curcumin, resveratrol, cannabidiol, gastrodin, and quercetin. Moreover, the complementary restoration of mitochondrial homeostasis through the modulation of downstream targets, such as transcription factor EB (TFEB) activation and BCL2-interacting protein 3-like (BNIP3L/NIX)-mediated mitophagy, is discussed as an indirect therapeutic strategy. Another important finding is that PD is a biologically and clinically heterogeneous disease that requires biomarker-directed and genotype-stratified therapeutic development. Finally, major translational issues are critically evaluated, including challenges related to blood-brain barrier penetration, target specificity, and long-term safety of mitochondrial modulators.

title: Facial emotion recognition of sadness relates to superior parietal gray matter volume in mild cognitive impairment.
abstract: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) is associated with early, regionally selective neurodegenerative changes that may affect socioemotional functioning before atrophy becomes widespread. This study examined whether structural brain alterations in MCI relate to facial emotion recognition performance. Sixty adults (30 MCI, 30 healthy controls), aged 50-86 years, completed neuropsychological testing, the Facial emotion composite Task, and structural MRI. Whole-brain voxel-based morphometry revealed no significant gray matter volume differences between groups. However, targeted region-of-interest ROI analyses demonstrated lower right amygdala and bilateral hippocampal volumes in patients with MCI. Cortical thickness analyses identified two regions with lower thickness in MCI: the right superior parietal lobule and the left posterior insula. A significant Group × Sadness interaction indicated that the association between left superior parietal gray matter volume and sadness recognition differed between groups. Follow-up analyses of the extracted values showed a positive association in MCI, although this within-group association did not reach statistical significance, and a significant inverse association in HCs. These findings suggest that early MCI involves selective thinning in association cortices supporting attention and salience processing. The sadness-specific interaction indicates that patients with MCI may rely on preserved superior parietal structure during sadness recognition, a pattern that is consistent with structural reserve accounts, although this interpretation remains speculative given the cross-sectional design.

title: Seizures Secondary to Aconitum Plant Poisoning: a case report.
abstract:
Aconitum plant poisoning typically manifests as isolated early cardiotoxicity or late neurotoxicity. However, the dynamic temporal evolution from arrhythmia-driven cardiogenic syncope to true epileptic seizures mediated by direct central nervous system injury remains rarely documented and poorly characterized.
We report a 53-year-old Han Chinese male who presented with ventricular tachycardia rapidly degenerating into ventricular fibrillation and cardiac arrest following ingestion of homemade Aconitum kusnezoffii (caowu)-infused liquor. Initial convulsions were tightly coupled with malignant arrhythmias, consistent with cardiogenic syncope. After successful resuscitation, hemoperfusion, and restoration of stable sinus rhythm, the patient developed breakthrough generalized tonic-clonic seizures on hospital days 4-6. Electroencephalography performed during sedation withdrawal revealed bilateral occipital spike-and-slow and sharp-and-slow waves with focal epileptiform discharges, confirming direct central nervous system neurotoxicity rather than recurrent cardiac ischemia. A mechanism-based, staged treatment strategy was employed: early advanced cardiac life support and hemoperfusion targeted cardiotoxicity, while sodium valproate and acetylglutamine were administered for antiepileptic prophylaxis and neuroprotection. The patient was discharged on day 13; antiepileptic therapy was successfully tapered and discontinued at 3 months without seizure recurrence, with normalization of electroencephalography and electrocardiography.
This case provides the first systematic documentation, validated by electroencephalography, of the transition from cardiogenic convulsions to true epileptic seizures in Aconitum alkaloid poisoning. The findings highlight the critical role of pharmacokinetic-driven central nervous system retention in delayed seizure onset and underscore the necessity of prolonged neurological monitoring, early electroencephalography evaluation for late-onset convulsions, and sustained antiepileptic prophylaxis to reduce mortality and long-term neurological sequelae.
Aconitum plant poisoning may manifest as early cardiogenic syncope and convulsions secondary to malignant arrhythmias, progressing in the late stage to genuine seizures caused by central nervous system (CNS) injury. Effective management requires a staged treatment strategy targeting both cardiotoxicity and neurotoxicity, with a focus on stabilizing cardiac rhythm and providing neuroprotection as needed.

title: Trajectory classes of post-stroke depression severity and their baseline predictors: A multi-cohort replication study.
abstract: Post-stroke depression (PSD) affects approximately one-third of stroke survivors and is associated with poorer rehabilitation outcomes, increased disability, and higher mortality. Despite its clinical importance, PSD is often studied as a binary outcome, obscuring heterogeneity in symptom trajectories over time. This study aimed to identify replicable longitudinal trajectories of PSD across independent cohorts and examine baseline predictors of trajectory membership. Data were analysed from three cohorts of the Stroke and Cognition Consortium (STROKOG; n = 750). Depressive symptoms were measured using the Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS-15) and the Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD-17). Latent class growth analysis was conducted within cohorts and in pooled GDS-15 and HAMD-17 datasets. Across six analyses, a consistent three-class solution emerged. The majority of participants (58-83%) showed no clinically significant depressive symptoms (No Depression). A second class (14-29%) displayed mild symptoms that generally remitted over time (Mild Remitting). A smaller subgroup (4-13%) exhibited symptoms in the moderate-severity range throughout follow-up, with trajectory direction varying across analyses. Baseline global cognitive impairment predicted Mild Remitting class membership across both pooled analyses. In pooled HAMD-17 analyses, female sex predicted membership in the Moderate Improving class, characterised by moderately severe symptoms that gradually resolved over time. In pooled GDS-15 analyses, older age, hypertension, and diabetes predicted membership in the Moderate Stable class. PSD follows a robust three-trajectory structure across independent cohorts, countries, and instruments. Early clinical factors, particularly cognitive impairment, sex, and vascular risk factors, may identify stroke survivors at risk for persistent depressive symptoms, enabling earlier targeted intervention.

title: Peripheral and cerebrospinal fluid inflammatory markers in sporadic amyotrophic lateral sclerosis an exploratory cross-sectional association study.
abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder with an ambiguous etiology, whose onset may be linked to innate immune system activation outside the central nervous system (CNS). We investigated the association between peripheral blood and CNS inflammatory parameters in 45 sporadic ALS patients compared to 30 controls, analyzing peripheral blood tests (C-reactive protein [CRP], blood count, fibrinogen) and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) immunological measures (Tumor Necrosis Factor alpha [TNF-α], TNF receptor type 1 [TNFR-1], CRP) alongside clinical characteristics. Results revealed significantly higher concentrations of TNFR-1 in the CSF of ALS patients compared to the control group (1,029.5 ± 176.0 vs. 846.1 ± 167.5 pg/ml; p < 0.0001). This difference remained significant in multivariable logistic regression adjusting for age and sex (OR 1.82 per 100 pg/ml increment, 95% CI 1.26-2.63; p = 0.0015). In an exploratory ROC analysis, CSF TNFR-1 discriminated patients from controls with an AUC of 0.78 (95% CI 0.67-0.88). TNFR-1 correlated with age (R = 0.32, p = 0.038), associations with disease severity and a lower concentration in bulbar-onset disease were exploratory and not robustly significant. Plasma and CSF CRP concentrations did not differ significantly between groups, but strongly correlated with each other in both ALS (R = 0.83) and control (R = 0.82) cohorts, indicating a disease-non-specific relationship. CSF TNFR-1 is independently associated with sporadic ALS and warrants further investigation as a candidate disease-associated inflammatory biomarker. Given the limitations, our findings do not prove diagnostic accuracy or causality. Longitudinal studies with disease controls and blood-CSF barrier integrity measures are needed.

title: Moyamoya disease presenting as galactorrhea.
abstract: Moyamoya disease (MMD) is a progressive cerebrovascular condition marked by carotid narrowing and collateral vessel formation. Patients are often diagnosed after a stroke, but here we describe a case of galactorrhea as the presenting symptom of MMD. A 30-year-old gravida 1, para 0 woman noted milky, nonbloody discharge leaking from both breasts after manual compression during sexual intercourse. Prolactin was mildly elevated at 29.4 ng/mL (SI [International System of Units]: 29.4 µg/L) (reference range, 3-23.1 ng/mL [SI: 3-23.1 µg/L]). Magnetic resonance imaging of the pituitary gland showed no microadenoma but incidentally revealed a tortuous right internal carotid artery compressing the pituitary, raising the possibility of vascular compression contributing to galactorrhea and mild hyperprolactinemia. Magnetic resonance angiography and catheter angiography confirmed MMD. Mild cognitive impairment, persistent headaches, and secondary hypertension eventually necessitated neurosurgical revascularization. After surgery, the patient experienced a significant reduction in symptoms although challenges with memory and headaches have persisted. This case underscores the importance of brain imaging in evaluating hyperprolactinemia and highlights the potential for endocrinologic sequelae when MMD involves vessels in proximity to the pituitary gland.

title: Somatostatin expression is associated with mitochondrial-related gene expression in a brain region-specific manner: Evidence from human transcriptomic analysis.
abstract:
Somatostatin (SST) is a critical neuropeptide whose deficiency is implicated in schizophrenia, major depressive disorder, and Alzheimer's disease. Mitochondrial dysfunction is a convergent pathological mechanism in these conditions. However, whether SST expression is associated with mitochondrial-related gene expression in the human brain remains unexplored.
We analyzed the GSE53987 dataset (n = 205 postmortem human brain samples across three regions: hippocampus, pre-frontal cortex, and associative striatum; four diagnostic groups: schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, major depressive disorder, and controls). SST expression was modeled as a continuous variable in linear regression models simultaneously adjusting for brain region, diagnosis, age, and sex. Analyses were performed both across all samples and within each brain region separately. Findings were examined for replication in GSE5281 (n = 161 non-demented control brain samples from six regions profiled by laser-capture microdissection).
After covariate adjustment, SST expression was significantly associated with BCL2 (adj.P = 6.49 × 10⁻⁴), MFN2 (adj.P = 1.76 × 10⁻³), and SOD2 (adj.P = 2.68 × 10⁻³). Brain region-stratified analyses revealed distinct patterns: hippocampus showed associations with SOD2, BCL2, and MFN2; pre-frontal cortex with BCL2, TFAM, ATP5A1, and PPARGC1A; associative striatum showed no significant associations. Analysis of GSE5281 showed similar region-specific SST-mitochondrial gene association patterns, with Superior Frontal Gyrus showing the strongest concordance (8/11 genes significant).
SST expression is associated with specific mitochondrial-related genes in a brain region-dependent manner. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant future experimental investigation of the SST-mitochondria relationship in neural tissue.

title: Falls induced by optogenetic inhibition of basal forebrain cholinergic neurons after dorsomedial striatal dopamine depletion in a dual disruption model of falling vulnerability in Parkinson's disease.
abstract: Falls are a common and debilitating feature of Parkinson's Disease (PD) patients. Prefrontal acetylcholine (ACh) deficits, as well as nigrostriatal dopamine deficits, are implicated in vulnerability to falls. PD patients with loss of cortical ACh and associated cognitive dysfunction experience a higher rate of falls than PD patients without cortical ACh loss. In addition, chemogenetic inhibition of basal forebrain (BF) neurons in rats increases the vulnerability to falls on a balance beam task. Here, the impact of transient optogenetic inhibition specifically of BF cholinergic neurons was assessed in rats with dorsomedial striatal dopamine lesions during traversal of straight or zig-zag balance beams using the Michigan Complex Movement Control Task (MCMCT). Adding transient optogenetic inhibition of BF cholinergic neurons with striatal dopamine lesions elevated falls above the level produced by striatal dopamine lesions or BF ACh inhibition alone, especially on the challenging zig-zag task. These results support the critical role of BF-cortical cholinergic circuits in alleviating vulnerability to falls in PD patients with striatal dopamine loss, suggesting that it is combined loss of BF cholinergic activity and striatal dopamine that leads to greatest vulnerability to falls and related complex movement impairments.

title: Associations of mild behavioral impairment and white matter hyperintensity patterns.
abstract:
It is unclear whether cerebrovascular and white matter changes contribute to mild behavioral impairment (MBI). White matter hyperintensities (WMHs) represent a prominent pathology for research due to association with cognitive decline. We investigated associations between MBI measures and WMH volume and spatial distribution.
We analyzed 1273 individuals with normal cognition or mild cognitive impairment. General linear models and voxel-wise analyses were employed to examine WMHs in terms of volume and spatial distribution.
Greater WMH volume was associated with higher MBI total score and MBI status in participants with normal cognition and mild cognitive impairment. Voxel-wise analysis revealed a significant cluster in the left inferior longitudinal fasciculus associated with higher MBI total score.
Our findings suggest a contribution of WMH volume and spatial distribution to persistent later-life behavioral symptoms. WMHs, especially in the left inferior longitudinal fasciculus, may serve as a neuroimaging marker of behavioral symptoms.

title: Projected burden of cold spell-attributable Parkinson's disease mortality among older adults in China under climate change and population ageing.
abstract: Population ageing may amplify cold-related health risks under climate change, particularly for older adults with Parkinson's disease (PD). We developed a climate-ageing projection framework to estimate the burden of cold spell-attributable PD mortality in China by integrating national mortality data, climate projections, and demographic forecasts. We analyzed 59,384 PD deaths among adults aged 60 years and older in China mainland during 2013-2020 using a time-stratified case-crossover design. Cold spells were associated with an increase in mortality, with effects concentrated within lags 0-4; the cumulative odds ratio was 1.109 (95% CI: 1.036, 1.187), with an attributable fraction (AF) of 9.83% (95% CI: 3.48%, 15.75%). AF point estimates were descriptively higher in southern than in northern China. Across the six administrative regions, AF point estimates ranged from -8.81% in Northwest China to 25.87% in Northeast China, with no statistical evidence of cross-region heterogeneity. Projections showed that cold spell-attributable PD mortality remained substantial across all scenarios in the 2030s, despite climate warming. Thereafter, trajectories diverged. Under SSP1-RCP2.6, projected nationwide attributable deaths were 744 (95% CI: -391, 1,659) in the 2030s, 988 (95% CI: -608, 2,277) in the 2050s, and 867 (95% CI: -589, 2,042) in the 2080s, with East and Southwest China contributing the largest shares and being the only regional estimates whose 95% CIs excluded zero. Under SSP2-RCP4.5, the nationwide burden rose modestly in the 2050s and then declined by the 2080s, whereas under SSP5-RCP8.5 it declined more steeply over time. These scenario-specific patterns occurred alongside substantial differences in projected cold spell occurrence, highlighting that future cold-related PD mortality cannot be inferred from mean warming alone. Under the modeled scenarios, climate warming did not necessarily translate into uniformly lower cold-related PD mortality in an ageing society. This persistence may warrant continued attention to cold-related risks in near-term climate-health adaptation for ageing populations.

title: EEG microstate dynamics across sleep stages in Alzheimer's disease: A pilot study.
abstract:
Alzheimer's disease (AD) is characterized by progressive cognitive decline and brain network dysfunction. EEG microstates offer a sight into rapid network dynamics. However, microstate alterations in AD during waking and different sleep stages remain unexplored.
Overnight EEG was recorded from 15 AD patients and 15 healthy controls. Sleep stages (Wake, N1, N2, N3, REM) were manually scored. Microstate analysis extracted temporal parameters and transition probabilities separately for each sleep stage using a common set of grand-mean template maps derived from all stages. Linear mixed models assessed group differences, and correlations examined associations with MMSE.
AD patients showed significantly longer durations compared to HC (Group main effect: F(1,28) = 6.78, p_FDR = 0.042) in mean duration of class A, with the largest difference during wakefulness (p = 0.018, q = 0.046). Mean occurrence of class D was significantly lower in AD (F(1,28) = 5.44, p_FDR = 0.049), with significant reductions during wakefulness and N1. Mean Occurrence of class C showed both a significant Group main effect (F(1,28) = 5.28, p_FDR = 0.049) and a Group × Sleep Stage interaction (F(4112) = 3.31, p_FDR = 0.047) were observed, with AD patients showing lower occurrence during wakefulness and N1. For transition probabilities, AD patients showed significantly increased corrected Class B→A transition (DeltaTM_B→A), but reduced corrected Class D→B transition (DeltaTM_D→B) and raw Class C→D transition (OrgTM_C→D) (all p_FDR < 0.05). Critically, the Group × Sleep Stage interaction for the corrected Class A→D transition (DeltaTM_A→D) reached significance (F(4112) = 6.12, p_FDR = 0.015), with the group difference largest during wakefulness (p = 0.004, q = 0.029). Partial correlations revealed that corrected B→A transition probability negatively correlated with MMSE (r = -0.642, p < 0.001); MeanOccurrence_C (r = 0.487, p = 0.003) and MeanOccurrence_D (r = 0.532, p = 0.001) also showed significant correlations with MMSE.
This is the first study to report that AD patients exhibit altered microstate parameters and transition probabilities across sleep stages. Present findings suggest that sleep-stage-resolved microstate analysis may offer a new tool for assessing AD.

title: Association of hypoxic burden with brain atrophy in Alzheimer's disease.
abstract:
Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA) is a common comorbidity in Alzheimer's Disease (AD) and may exacerbate neurodegeneration. This study investigates the association between a novel metric of OSA severity-hypoxic burden (HB)-and measures of AD-related neurodegeneration.
In this retrospective exploratory study, patients with AD at stage 3 and stage 4 (NIA-AA 2018 criteria), enrolled at a Center for Neurodegenerative Diseases, underwent a complete sleep assessment including polysomnography and 3 T brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging. Correlation analyses were conducted between HB and brain volumes.
Twenty-two patients (36.4% males, mean age 69.8 ± 7.5) were enrolled. OSA was diagnosed in 40.9% of patients. HB inversely correlated with left hippocampus (ρ = -0.553, p = 0.02) and left amygdala (ρ = -0.496, p = 0.04) volumes. AD patients with OSA showed significantly reduced left hippocampal volume than those without OSA (p = 0.038).
This study highlights that greater OSA severity, measured by HB, correlates with left hippocampus and amygdala atrophy, suggesting a possible association between chronic hypoxia and neurodegeneration in AD.

title: Therapeutic Potential and Toxicological Trade-Offs of Nanoparticle-Enhanced Valproic Acid in Glioblastoma: Behavioral and Oxidative Insights.
abstract:
Glioblastoma (GBM) is a highly aggressive brain tumor with a poor prognosis. In the current research, the therapeutic and behavioral efficacy of valproic acid (VPA) and its nanoparticles (Nano VPA) with or without temozolomide (TMZ) was investigated in the C6 glioblastoma rat model.
We divided eighty-four adult male Wistar rats into seven groups (n=12/group): sham, tumor, TMZ, VPA, nano VPA, VPA + TMZ, and nano VPA + TMZ. To induce tumors, C6 cells were injected into the brains of the rats. On days 12 to 15, behavioral performance was assessed using the social interaction test, elevated plus maze, open field, rotarod, and passive avoidance. On day 18, tumor size, edema, and histopathology were examined. Oxidative stress parameters in brain tissue and serum were measured by ELISA.
VPA and Nano VPA significantly inhibited tumor growth, either alone or with TMZ. All treatments except Nano VPA + TMZ improved survival compared with tumor controls. Treated groups showed enhanced anxiety regulation, sociability, learning, and memory. Motor coordination improved following VPA or Nano VPA therapy. Tumor induction reduced serum SOD, CAT, and TAC levels; treatments raised serum TAC and lowered brain MDA, but further reduced serum SOD.
Our results suggest that oxidative stress modulation may contribute to the neurobehavioral and antitumor effects of both VPA and nano-VPA. While nano-VPA showed greater tumor reduction, conventional VPA was more effective in improving survival. Combining VPA with TMZ may enhance outcomes, and support further study of Nano VPA as an adjuvant therapy for GBM.

title: Mediating role of sleep in the association between HIV infection and depression: a cross-sectional analysis with NHANES data.
abstract: Depression is a major public health concern and frequently coexists with sleep disturbances, particularly among individuals with Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) infection. However, it remains unclear to what extent sleep disturbance may account for the observed association between HIV infection and depressive symptoms. This study examined the associations among HIV infection, sleep status, and depressive symptoms and assessed the potential contribution of sleep status. Using data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2005-2014 cycles, weighted logistic regression, Firth's penalized regression, Bayesian mediation analysis, and LightGBM with SHAP interpretation were applied. Among 14444 adults, HIV-positive status was associated with higher odds of depressive symptoms, but the association was attenuated and became non-significant after adjustment for demographic, socioeconomic, and behavioral factors. Sleep quality showed a graded association with depression, with ORs of 2.17, 5.83, and 13.60 for fair, poor, and very poor sleep. Bayesian mediation analysis suggested that sleep disturbance may explain the association between HIV infection and depressive symptoms. SHAP analysis identified sleep status as the most important predictor of depression. These findings highlight the importance of sleep assessment and management for improving mental health among individuals with HIV infection.

title: Measuring LGBTQ-affirmative therapist behavior: Development of the LGBTQ Affirmation and Discussion In-Session (LADI) Inventory.
abstract:
The within-session processes that constitute LGBTQ-affirmative psychotherapy remain under-specified.
We developed and validated an observational measure of therapists' LGBTQ affirmation and discussion in-session (LADI) in a study of 57 gay and bisexual men who received 10 sessions of treatment-as-usual in two LGBTQ community organizations as part of a larger trial.
Independent raters reliably agreed on the presence of LGBTQ affirmation and discussion in sessions when using the LADI. Even when controlling for the therapeutic alliance, clients exhibited greater change in observer-rated depressive symptoms, self-reported substance use consequences, and internalized heterosexism when they had a therapist who displayed more LGBTQ affirmation on the LADI, although results for internalized heterosexism may have been sensitive to an outlier. The LADI did not predict changes in HIV-risk-transmission behavior, alcohol use, anxiety symptoms, suicidal ideation, rejection sensitivity, sexual orientation concealment, or identity affirmation.
The LADI can facilitate future research on LGBTQ-affirmative psychotherapy.

title: DTI-ALPS index and cognitive performance in temporal lobe epilepsy with and without hippocampal sclerosis: A cross-sectional study.
abstract:
Temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) often involves cognitive impairment, with hippocampal sclerosis (HS) as a key pathology. Although neuronal loss and proteinopathy are established mechanisms, the role of perivascular clearance pathways remains underexplored in TLE.
This retrospective, single-centre cross-sectional study included 212 participants aged 24-71 years: 79 patients with TLE and visually identified unilateral hippocampal sclerosis, 57 patients with TLE without hippocampal sclerosis, and 76 healthy controls. We aimed to compare the DTI‑ALPS index-an indirect diffusion‑derived index that may be associated with perivascular‑related processes-and its association with cognition in TLE with and without HS.
After adjusting for age, sex, and education, the global ALPS index was significantly lower in TLE‑HS than in TLE‑non‑HS and HC (both p < 0.05), and also lower in TLE‑non‑HS than in HC ( p < 0.01). For right‑hemispheric ALPS, both patient groups were lower than HC ( p < 0.01), but TLE‑HS and TLE‑non‑HS did not differ significantly ( p = 0.12). Left‑hemispheric ALPS was lower in TLE‑HS than in the other two groups ( p < 0.05), whereas TLE‑non‑HS and HC did not differ (p = 0.08). Cognitive performance showed that TLE‑HS performed worse than both other groups on all measures (all p < 0.05); TLE‑non‑HS performed worse than HC on MoCA, AVLT, SDMT and SCWT ( p < 0.05) but not on TMT(B‑A) ( p = 0.08). Within‑group partial correlations with FDR correction (q < 0.05) revealed significant associations between the ALPS index and MoCA, SDMT, and TMT(B‑A) in the TLE‑HS group; with SCWT in the TLE‑non‑HS group; and with SDMT in the HC group.
The DTI‑ALPS index was lower in patients with TLE, particularly those with visually classified HS, and was associated with selected cognitive measures in a group‑specific manner. No formal statistical comparison of correlation strength across groups was performed. Because DTI‑ALPS is an indirect diffusion‑derived index and the study was cross‑sectional, these findings do not establish causality or a biological mechanism. Further longitudinal studies using direct measures of cerebrospinal fluid dynamics are required.

title: Pearls & Oy-sters: DPPX Antibody-Associated Encephalitis in a Patient With Diarrhea, Tremor, Ocular Flutter, and Cognitive-Psychiatric Changes.
abstract: Dipeptidyl-peptidase-like protein-6 antibody-associated encephalitis (DPPXE) is an autoimmune, multisystem disorder characterized by a triad of gastrointestinal prodrome, cognitive-psychiatric change, and CNS hyperexcitability. We report a 57-year-old man with 2 months of progressive gastrointestinal symptoms despite extensive normal gastrointestinal evaluation. He then developed tremor, myoclonus, gait ataxia, hyperekplexia, insomnia, emotional lability, memory impairment, and abnormal eye movements. Examination showed ocular flutter, tremor, ataxia, and cognitive impairment. Brain MRI revealed bilateral T2/fluid-attenuated inversion recovery hyperintensities in the brainstem and limbic regions. CSF demonstrated lymphocytic pleocytosis and 10 unique oligoclonal bands. DPPX-immunoglobulin G was detected in serum and CSF, confirming the diagnosis of DPPXE. Acute immunotherapy with intravenous methylprednisolone and plasma exchange followed by maintenance treatment with rituximab led to dramatic improvement of his symptoms, with residual memory impairment and tremor at 3 months. This case underscores the characteristic gastrointestinal prodrome and syndromic breadth of DPPXE, highlights the diagnostic value of panel-based screening, and supports treatment with immunomodulation.

title: Feasibility of High-Intensity Interval Exercise in Young Adult Survivors of Pediatric Brain Tumor and Young Adults With Isocitrate Dehydrogenase-Mutant Gliomas (HYPE): Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract:
Young adult survivors of pediatric brain tumors and young adult patients with isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) mutant gliomas are at risk for cognitive impairment, reduced physical fitness and function, as well as poor health-related quality of life (HRQOL) and psychosocial health. Exercise improves these outcomes; however, both populations remain understudied with respect to exercise interventions. High-intensity interval training (HIIT) is a promising intervention, as it is time-efficient, safe, tolerable, enhances cognition in healthy young adults, and improves physical fitness and quality of life in adult patients and survivors with cancer. However, the feasibility of HIIT is not yet understood in survivors of pediatric brain tumors and patients with IDH-mutant glioma.
The HYPE study is a pilot randomized controlled trial that aims to (1) determine the feasibility of a HIIT exercise intervention for young adult survivors of pediatric brain tumors and patients with IDH-mutant glioma, (2) determine the preliminary efficacy of HIIT to improve physical fitness and function, cognition, HRQOL, and psychosocial health, and (3) explore exercise sustainability and the impact of social determinants of health on study outcomes.
A total of 30 young adult survivors of pediatric brain tumors and patients with IDH-mutant glioma (18-45 years of age) will be randomized to an exercise or control group. The exercise group performs virtually supervised HIIT 3 times per week for 16 weeks, followed by 16 weeks of self-directed exercise. Exercise involves indoor cycling, and sessions include 20 minutes of high- and low-intensity intervals (high intensity=60-s 60%-90% peak power output; low intensity=60-s 10% peak power output), and a 5-minute warm-up and cool-down. The control group performs a 16-week stretching program. Feasibility of the HIIT intervention is measured by the number of exercise sessions completed, including total minutes and intensity, and barriers to exercise adherence. Cognition, physical fitness and function, HRQOL, and psychosocial health are measured using standardized assessments and self-report questionnaires. Exercise sustainability is measured by change in study outcomes following the self-directed follow-up period, and social determinants of health are assessed using a self-report questionnaire.
Baseline data collection began in February 2024, and 13 participants have been enrolled as of June 2026. The projected study end date is December 2026. Data analysis is planned to begin in January 2027, and findings will be published in the fall of 2028.
To our knowledge, this study is the first to use a virtually supervised HIIT intervention in young adult patients and survivors of brain tumor. The findings will elucidate the feasibility of HIIT to design and power a randomized controlled trial to address cancer- and treatment-related sequelae. They will also provide insights into the sustainability of HIIT and the impact of social determinants of health.

title: Doxepin Attenuates Cognitive and Anxiety-like Behavioral Deficits Induced by Acute Kidney Injury in Rats.
abstract:
Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a systemic disorder with consequences extending beyond the kidney, including central nervous system dysfunction. Clinical and experimental evidence indicates that AKI is associated with cognitive impairment and neuropsychiatric disturbances. However, effective strategies to prevent or attenuate AKI-associated brain dysfunction are lacking. Doxepin, a tricyclic antidepressant, exhibits neuroprotective properties that may counteract key mechanisms implicated in AKI-induced neural injury.
In this study, acute renal failure (ARF) was used as an experimental model of AKI. ARF was induced in male Wistar rats through glycerol injection. Animals were allocated into four experimental groups: Control, doxepin (DOX), ARF, or ARF-DOX. Doxepin was given orally at a dose of 5 mg/kg once daily over a 12-day period. Renal function was assessed using serum and urinary urea measurements. Anxiety-related behavior was assessed using the open field test and the elevated plus maze, whereas spatial learning and memory were evaluated with the radial arm water maze.
Glycerol-induced ARF resulted in significant alterations in urinary parameters, including reduced urinary urea concentration and increased urine output and flow rate, while serum urea levels did not differ significantly among groups. ARF did not impair spatial learning acquisition but significantly disrupted short- and long-term memory retention. In addition, ARF induced specific anxiety-like behavioral alterations, including increased freezing behavior, reduced rearing activity, and decreased open-arm entries in anxiogenic environments. Doxepin treatment significantly attenuated memory impairments and partially normalized anxiety-related behaviors, without improving biochemical markers of renal dysfunction.
These findings demonstrate that AKI induces selective cognitive and anxiety-like behavioral deficits and support the existence of a kidney-brain axis. Doxepin attenuated AKI-associated neurobehavioral impairments.
This study supports the potential repurposing of doxepin, an established clinically used and brain-penetrant drug, as a therapeutic strategy for attenuating AKI-associated neurobehavioral dysfunction.

title: Embodiment, Enaction, and Attunement in Schizophrenia, Autism, and Psychopathy: A Comparative Phenomenological Review.
abstract: Schizophrenia spectrum disorders, autism spectrum disorder, and psychopathy may resemble one another at the behavioural surface. All three may involve social difficulties, flattened or atypical affect, unusual communication, interpersonal friction, and impaired social adaptation. Yet their experiential architectures differ in ways that are clinically decisive for differential diagnosis, risk assessment, therapeutic alliance, and environmental design. This narrative review critically synthesizes work in phenomenological psychopathology and 4E cognitive science to clarify how embodiment, enaction, and attunement are altered across these conditions, with attention to lived space, lived time, selfhood, the Other, empathy, and atmosphere. We draw on classical phenomenological psychopathology, contemporary research on minimal self disturbance and anomalous self and world experience, enactive and participatory sense-making accounts of social cognition, and theoretical and empirical literature on autism and psychopathy. Schizophrenia is characterised by instability of minimal self and world openness, including hyperreflexivity, diminished self-affection, altered salience, temporal fragmentation, demarcation disturbances, and atmospheric shifts that may precede overt psychosis. Autism is characterised by differences in embodied sense-making and interactional coordination, frequently involving sensory regulation needs, altered social timing, atypical affordance perception, masking fatigue, and bidirectional mismatch as described by the double empathy problem. Psychopathy is characterised by preserved strategic social understanding with reduced affective resonance, moral emotions, and interpersonal concern, yielding forms of instrumental attunement and distinctive encounter climates. Clinically, targeted phenomenological and second person assessment can improve formulation, reduce diagnostic overshadowing, and guide more differentiated care pathways.

title: Neuropsychological performance, past-month active suicidal ideation, and lifetime suicide attempt history in individuals with psychosis: A cross-sectional study.
abstract:
Individuals with psychosis have elevated suicide risk and neuropsychological dysfunction. Prior research on neurocognition and suicidality in psychosis is mixed, with better cognition linked to both greater and lower history of suicide ideation (SI) and suicide attempts (SA). The current study examined associations between neuropsychological performance, demographics, psychiatric symptoms, past month SI, and lifetime SA history in individuals with psychosis.
235 adults with schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, or bipolar disorder with psychotic features completed clinical interviews, neuropsychological assessment, and symptom measures (positive and negative symptoms; depressive symptoms). Participants were grouped by past month active SI (SI+; n = 110) versus passive/no SI (SI-; n = 125) and lifetime actual SA history (SA+; n = 152) versus no SA (SA-; n = 83). Among SA + participants, we examined lifetime aborted attempts, interrupted attempts, preparatory behaviors, and attempt lethality. False Discovery Rate correction was used for multiple comparisons.
SI + individuals reported more severe depressive and positive symptoms; only depressive symptoms uniquely predicted SI. SA + individuals were significantly older and had worse working memory and processing speed than SA-individuals, but only age uniquely predicted SA history. Those with aborted attempt history demonstrated better premorbid intellectual functioning and working memory; only working memory remained significant in the multivariable model. After FDR correction, there were no significant predictors of interrupted attempts, preparatory behavior, or attempt lethality.
Current SI may be more closely associated with symptoms, whereas better working memory may be associated with aborting a suicide attempt.

title: Feature selection and dimensionality reduction in multi-omics.
abstract: High-throughput multi-omics technologies generate high-dimensional, heterogeneous and noisy datasets, making robust biomarker discovery and disease modelling challenging. This review critically examines dimensionality reduction and representation strategies for multi-omics analysis while distinguishing three related but different goals: feature selection, feature extraction/representation learning, and multi-omics integration. We use sparse canonical correlation analysis (sCCA), variational autoencoders (VAEs), and graph convolutional networks (GCNs) as representative case studies spanning sparse linear, probabilistic deep-learning, and graph-based approaches. Rather than treating these methods as interchangeable, we compare their data requirements, assumptions, interpretability, ability to accommodate non-linearity and missing modalities, computational demands, and validation needs. Applications across cancer, cardiovascular and neurodegenerative disease, and across bulk, single-cell, spatial and imaging multi-omics are summarized in comparative tables. We conclude with practical guidance for matching method families to biological questions and emphasize that robust biomarker claims require leakage-free model development, stability assessment and independent validation.

title: Effects of visual remediation on contour integration performance in schizophrenia spectrum disorders.
abstract:
Impairments in visual processing, including difficulties in perceptual organization, are well documented in schizophrenia and related serious mental illnesses. These impairments are thought to contribute to reductions in higher-order cognition and functioning. The present study examined whether a visual remediation intervention targeting low- and mid-level visual processing improves perceptual organization in this population.
Participants with schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder were randomized to visual remediation (VR) or an active control (AC) condition. The VR intervention targeted contrast sensitivity and contour integration, and perceptual organization was assessed using the Jittered Orientation Visual Integration (JOVI) task. Primary analyses focused on participants who completed the task at baseline, mid-treatment, and post-treatment (N = 50; VR: n = 26; AC: n = 24). Linear mixed-effects models examined JOVI performance as a function of treatment condition, timepoint, and task difficulty (jitter), with planned contrasts testing differential change over time.
A significant treatment condition × timepoint interaction indicated that changes in performance differed between groups. Planned difference-in-differences contrasts showed that the VR group exhibited greater improvement from baseline to mid-treatment (estimate = 5.03, p < .001) and from baseline to post-treatment (estimate = 4.30, p = .005) relative to AC.
VR targeting low- and mid-level visual processes improved perceptual organization performance relative to an AC condition in participants with a schizophrenia spectrum disorder. These effects emerged early in training and persisted to the post-treatment assessment, supporting the effectiveness of interventions targeting visual processes for improving perceptual organization in this population.

title: An integrative transcriptomic atlas of ALS and aging skeletal muscle defines shared and distinct molecular programs of degeneration.
abstract: Skeletal muscle atrophy and weakness resulting from loss of motor neuron innervation are shared hallmarks of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and age-associated sarcopenia. However, muscle wasting in ALS is rapid and severe, whereas sarcopenia progresses gradually over decades, peaking at an advanced age. The molecular mechanisms underlying muscle wasting in these conditions remain incompletely defined. Here, we used the SOD1G93A ALS mouse model and wild-type mice across the lifespan to generate an integrated single-nucleus transcriptomic atlas of skeletal muscle, mapping changes associated with ALS and aging. This atlas is complemented by structural and functional analyses. Our results identify transcriptionally distinct condition-specific myonuclear states, including disease-responsive programs within synaptic myonuclei at the neuromuscular junction, that are shared or distinct between the two conditions. Notably, at early stages, muscle from ALS mice exhibits molecular hallmarks of aged muscle at the myofiber level, indicating premature aging and reinforcing aging as a risk factor in ALS. At advanced disease stages and in old age, myonuclear subpopulations follow similar degenerative pathways in fast glycolytic fibers, consistent with their loss in both conditions. However, a distinct ALS-enriched myonuclei subpopulation displays uniquely regulated genes not observed in aged muscle, potentially underlying the more rapid and severe pathology observed in ALS. This atlas maps shared and divergent mechanisms of muscle degeneration in ALS and sarcopenia and provides a resource for identifying therapeutic targets tailored to each condition.

title: Exploring the pharmacological basis of adverse effects in oxazolidinone and antidepressant cotherapy: an in silico study.
abstract: Linezolid and related oxazolidinones are frontline antibiotics against multidrug-resistant Gram-positive pathogens, including methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), yet their co-administration with antidepressants has been clinically associated with serotonin syndrome (SS) or hypertensive crisis (HC). While traditionally attributed to monoamine oxidase (MAO) inhibition, clinical observations remain variable and the underlying mechanism is not completely understood. In this exploratory study, we applied an integrated in silico framework combining target prediction, network similarity, and structural modeling to generate testable hypotheses regarding potential alternative targets. Consensus profiling using SwissTargetPrediction and an integrative structural- and physicochemical-based target prediction methodology predicted possible interactions of linezolid and tedizolid with MAO isoforms, alongside exploratory aminergic targets including the 5-HT1A (HTR1A) receptor and adrenergic clusters. Comparing predicted targets with clinical datasets revealed an overlap with genes associated with SS and HC. Pathway enrichment and Jaccard similarity showed notable functional convergence with sertraline (OC > 0.90). Structural comparisons and physicochemical clustering grouped oxazolidinones near neurotransmitter intermediates, such as N-acetylserotonin. Furthermore, molecular docking across multiple crystallographic structures and ligand efficiency (LE) estimations suggested theoretically favorable interactions within MAO and HTR1A binding pockets, supported by shared pharmacophoric features. These computational findings provide a preliminary, hypothesis-generating basis suggesting that oxazolidinone-induced toxicity may involve targets beyond MAO, highlighting HTR1A modulation as a candidate mechanism requiring dedicated in vitro and in vivo validation.

title: Bi-allelic variants in the secretory pathway gene SEC16A are associated with a neurodevelopmental disorder.
abstract: SEC16A encodes a scaffold protein that organizes the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) exit sites, specialized ER subdomains that mediate export of newly synthesized proteins and regulate early secretory pathway steps. The role of SEC16A in human nervous system diseases has not been established yet. Here, we report six individuals with bi-allelic SEC16A variants who presented with early-onset neurological symptoms, including cognitive impairment, motor delays, and seizures. Using Drosophila, we show the Sec16 ortholog is essential for normal development and that its loss causes early lethality. Neuron-specific knockdown of Sec16 causes neurological phenotypes including locomotor defects, seizure-like bang sensitivity, and impaired synaptic transmission, which can be associated with the clinical features observed in affected individuals. Neurons differentiated from patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) carrying SEC16A variants display reduced SEC16A protein, impaired neurite outgrowth and increased excitability, which are rescued in isogenic control neurons when the variants are corrected, consistent with a loss-of-function mechanism. Increased ER stress was observed in both patient iPSC-derived neurons and fly models. In summary, our findings indicate a conserved requirement for SEC16A in neurodevelopment and neuronal function and implicate ER stress as a key cellular phenotype underlying the SEC16A-associated neurodevelopmental disorder.

title: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists for Mood Disorders and Suicide Risk.
abstract: Identifying innovative mechanisms that translate into improved therapeutics when compared to the extant options is a strategic imperative in mood disorders. More specifically, there is a need for treatments with greater efficacy, shorter time-to-peak efficacy, greater durability of effect, and improved tolerability profiles. Moreover, priority has also shifted toward identifying mood disorder therapeutics capable of targeting domains of psychopathology that are most pervasive, debilitating, and inadequately treated by conventional pharmacology (e.g., anhedonia and cognitive impairment). Available preclinical, translational, observational, and clinical data suggest that glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) hold promise as potentially mechanistically informed therapeutics for people with mood disorders. Although metabolic effectors are implicated as a putative mechanism of action of GLP-1RAs, nonmutually exclusive targets also include direct effects on neuroplasticity, neurogenesis, neurodifferentiation, neuroprotection, antiapoptotic, and autophagy mechanisms. Available evidence supports the initiation of adequate and well-controlled clinical studies in both major depressive disorder and bipolar disorder as acute and/or maintenance treatments. Although associations between suicidality and GLP-1RAs have been reported, causality has not been established. Moreover, preliminary evidence suggests that GLP-1RAs may benefit aspects of mood disorder psychopathology (e.g., reward) that may be predictive of potential beneficial effects on aspects of suicidality.

title: A unified general cognitive factor explains impairment across schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, OCD and substance use disorder.
abstract:
Emerging evidence suggests that cognitive impairment cuts across traditional psychiatric diagnoses and may reflect a shared underlying cognitive liability. We examined whether a general cognitive factor (gFc) accounts for transdiagnostic deficits across schizophrenia (SZ), bipolar disorder (BD), obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) and substance use disorder (SUD).
A total of 797 individuals [544 affected and 253 healthy controls (HC)] completed a standardized cognitive battery. Bifactor confirmatory factor analysis was used to derive general cognitive factor (gFc) and domain-specific impairments (cognitive flexibility, working memory, new learning and social cognition). Model fit supported the bifactor structure. Linear mixed-effect models, with family as random effect, and demographic variables as fixed effect evaluated transdiagnostic and diagnosis specific impairments.
The gFc was significantly reduced across all diagnoses groups relative to HC, [B(SE): BD -0.49 (0.07), OCD -0.21 (0.07), SUD -0.43(0.08), SZ -0.76 (0.08), all p < 0.001]; verbal learning showed additional diagnosis-specific deficits, most pronounced in SZ [B (SE):0.59 (0.09)] and BD[B(SE):0.48 (0.09)], both p < 0.001.
A single gFc accounts for substantial cognitive dysfunction across major psychiatric disorders, while verbal-learning impairment appears diagnosis-specific. These findings support a dimensional architecture of cognition in psychiatry and identify gFc as a promising transdiagnostic target for clinical and mechanistic research.

title: Examinations of the heterogeneity in the structural brain connectome in schizophrenia.
abstract:
Schizophrenia (SCZ) is a heterogeneous disorder characterized by widespread brain dysconnectivity, yet it remains unclear whether variable structural dysconnectivity patterns reflect biologically and clinically meaningful subtypes.
We recruited 105 SCZ patients and 97 healthy controls, collecting magnetic resonance imaging, clinical assessment, and laboratory test data. Double generalized linear models were first applied to estimate group differences in the mean and inter-individual variability of structural connectivity between SCZ and controls. Subsequently, nonnegative matrix factorization was used to identify SCZ subtypes according to dysconnectivity profiles.
We observed a significantly altered subnetwork that exhibited increased inter-individual variability in SCZ, with its connections and regions predominantly enriched in the ventral-attention, frontal-parietal, and default-mode networks that support higher-order cognition. Connectivity-derived subtype analysis grouped patients into two subtypes, with subtype-II tending to show more severe positive symptoms (t = 2.272, nominal P = 0.025), a lower neutrophil/lymphocyte ratio (t = -2.383, nominal P = 0.025), a better treatment response (t = 2.366, nominal P = 0.021), and greater short-term symptom improvement (t = 3.509, nominal P = 0.006) within the olanzapine monotherapy subgroup. This subtype also demonstrated distinct neuroanatomical features, including a subtype-specific cortical thickness change pattern unrelated to SCZ or bipolar disorder, as well as subtype-specific brain epicenters, such as left posterior cingulate and rostral middle frontal regions.
Our study demonstrates increased inter-individual variability in the structural connectome of SCZ and highlights the potential of connectome-based subtyping approaches for characterizing disease heterogeneity related to pathophysiological processes.

title: Preliminary comparison of four factor structures of facial emotion recognition in individuals with schizophrenia.
abstract:
Individuals with schizophrenia tend to have moderate-to-severe deficits in facial emotion recognition. To characterize the deficits and inform future interventions, measures with robust structural validity are needed. Four structures have been proposed: the 7-domain structure (happiness, sadness, anger, disgust, fear, surprise, and neutral), the 1-domain structure (an overall ability), the 2-domain structure (threatening and non-threatening faces, with surprise excluded), and the 4-domain structure (positive, negative, unexpected, and neutral). This study compared the four candidate structures of facial emotion recognition in individuals with schizophrenia.
Data from 351 Asian adults with schizophrenia were obtained from projects validating social cognition measures. Confirmatory factor analysis was used to examine the four candidate structures using odd-even and first-and-second-half item parceling approaches. Robust maximum likelihood estimation was additionally used as a sensitivity analysis.
Under maximum likelihood estimation, only the 7-domain structure achieved satisfactory model fit across parceling approaches (χ²/df = 1.8 and 1.2; comparative fit index = 0.977 and 0.995; root-mean-square error of approximation = 0.049 and 0.023; standardized root-mean-square residual = 0.032 and 0.028). The preference for emotion-specific scoring remained unchanged under robust maximum likelihood estimation and in additional comparisons restricted to the six facial emotion recognition categories common to all candidate structures.
Separate domain scores for each emotion may be preferable. Facial emotion recognition measures could include six basic emotions and neutral faces to support comprehensive emotion-specific score interpretation. However, these preliminary, population-dependent findings require validation in non-Asian populations.
